- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% to match true mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days to align with mean reversion.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.80) and model forecasts are rising, check for overconfidence bias — cap upward trend at +5% above recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.27–0.53) and price is trending down, model often underestimates fall; add 1–2% downward bias to forecast to avoid lag.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates early drops or late recoveries; apply smoothing filter: average last 5 forecast values before final output.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to ignore sentiment and overreact to noise — reduce forecast volatility by 20–30% in such cases.
